entities.summary:
Otho Holand was a prominent English soldier and a founder Knight of the Garter, who played a significant role in the establishment of the Order of the Garter in 1348. 

Born into a noble family, Holand was educated at the University of Oxford and later served as a knight in the English army during the Hundred Years' War. He participated in several key battles, including the Battle of Crécy, and was awarded the Order of the Garter for his bravery and loyalty. 

As a result of his actions, the Order of the Garter became a prestigious honor, bestowed upon knights who demonstrated exceptional military prowess and chivalry. Holand's legacy as a founder of the Order has endured for centuries, with the Garter still being awarded to distinguished individuals today.

The Garter's influence extended beyond England, shaping the chivalric ideals of the medieval world. The Order's emphasis on loyalty, honor, and military service resonated with nobles across Europe, contributing to the rise of the chivalric code. 

Holland's impact on the Garter's legacy can be seen in the many notable knights who followed in his footsteps, including King Edward III, who wore the Garter as a symbol of his royal authority. 

In conclusion, Otho Holand's contributions to the establishment and evolution of the Order of the Garter have left a lasting impact on the history of chivalry and knighthood. His legacy continues to be felt today, with the Garter remaining an important symbol of British honor and tradition.
